title: Higher-harmonic spin-wave excitation by a superconducting antenna with vortices
authors: Anton Pokusinskyi, Paweł Gruszecki, Julia Kharlan, Oleksandr Dobrovolskiy, Jarosław W. Kłos
abstract: The interaction between superconductivity and magnetism provides new routes for controlling nonlinear excitations in hybrid systems. While dc-driven Abrikosov vortices (fluxons) are known to interact with spin waves, the ability of confined, nearly harmonic vortex oscillations to generate higher-frequency spin-wave modes remains unexplored. Here, by combining time-dependent Ginzburg--Landau modeling with spectral analysis of the microwave near field, we demonstrate higher-harmonic spin-wave excitation driven by a superconducting microstrip antenna in the Shubnikov phase. Unlike conventional harmonic-generation mechanisms associated with nonlinear magnetization dynamics, the magnetic layer remains a linear receiver, whereas the superconducting antenna generates the nonlinear microwave field. We show that nearly sinusoidal vortex motion and the accompanying redistribution of superconducting screening currents produce higher harmonics that couple to spin-wave modes. This response arises from spatial-to-temporal transduction, whereby harmonic vortex motion and the associated redistribution of screening currents convert a spatially nonuniform magnetic-field profile into higher temporal harmonics. Magnetic flux quanta thus act as active nonlinear elements for frequency conversion, extending the accessible spin-wave frequency range in superconducting--magnonic hybrids.
summary: This work demonstrates that superconducting vortices can act as active nonlinear sources to generate higher harmonics in the microwave field. These harmonics then efficiently excite spin waves in an adjacent magnetic film, proving that the superconducting element drives the nonlinear frequency conversion, while the magnetic layer remains a linear detector.
main_problem: The study investigates generating higher-harmonic spin-wave excitations in a magnetic film using a superconducting antenna containing Abrikosov vortices.
main_result: Higher harmonics are generated via spatial-to-temporal transduction from the vortex motion in the SC antenna, allowing the magnetic layer to act as a linear receiver for frequency conversion.
method: The authors combine time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau modeling for the superconducting dynamics with micromagnetic simulations (Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation) for the magnetic layer.
model_or_system: The system is a hybrid structure: a superconducting microstrip antenna (e.g., Lead) coupled to a magnetic film (e.g., Ga:YIG) containing Abrikosov vortices. The SC dynamics are governed by TDGL, while the magnetization dynamics use LLG.
key_observables: Higher-harmonic spin-wave excitation (at $2f, 3f, \dots$), the frequency–wave-vector Fourier amplitude spectrum of magnetization.
important_parameters: Drive frequency ($f=12$ GHz), bias field ($B_0 = 30$ mT), SC material ($	ext{Pb}$), and magnetic material ($	ext{Ga:YIG}$).
main_assumptions: The magnetic layer is treated as a linear receiver of the nonlinear microwave field generated by the SC antenna, and vortex motion is assumed to be nearly harmonic.
figures_summary: Schematics illustrate the geometry and the physical process: Lorentz force drives vortex oscillations, leading to non-sinusoidal stray fields that generate higher harmonics exciting spin waves.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical setup and problem, details the theoretical modeling using TDGL and LLG equations, presents the simulation parameters and analysis techniques (e.g., Fourier transforms), and concludes with the demonstration of higher-harmonic excitation.
why_interesting: The concept of using superconducting flux quanta as active nonlinear elements for frequency conversion bridges superconducting physics, nonlinear dynamics, and magnonics, which has implications for advanced quantum sensing and energy transfer.
